key_insight: Rear-face angle affects turbulence most strongly when the separated flow still interacts with the trailing edge; once upper-surface reattachment occurs, protrusion length mainly controls the flow topology and production levels.
engineering_relevance: Designing surface-mounted features with the right length and rear-face angle can tune separation, reattachment, and near-wall turbulence production in boundary-layer flows.
method: Stereo particle image velocimetry over 12 trapezoidal protrusions
Tested L/h = 1, 2, 3, 4 with rear-face angles of 30°, 45°, and 90°
Compared flow topology and decomposed deviatoric production into magnitude and orientation effects
evidence_signal: Experiments were performed at Reynolds number ≈5×10^4 with boundary-layer thickness comparable to protrusion height, revealing topology changes from connected reverse flow to reattachment as L/h increased.
watch_item: The results are specific to the tested Reynolds number range and geometry set, so extrapolation to different boundary layers or protrusion shapes should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Flow separation and turbulence production over trapezoidal protrusions
